assignmentScope: Grade 3 multiplication as equal groups: number of groups x amount in each group
Equal-group and array representations read or constructed, not merely decorated
Mapping a representation to a multiplication equation and product
Factor meaning: which factor counts groups and which counts items per group
Factors constrained to 1-10, products at or below 100
Excluded from scoring: reading fluency, spelling, typing speed, pointer precision, computation beyond the stated factor range

constructs.name: Equal-group structure recognition
constructs.definition: Given a described or shown situation of equal groups, the child identifies that the situation is multiplicative and states the number of groups and the amount in each group.
prerequisites: Recognizing that groups are equal in size
constructs.observableBehavior: Child reports a (groups, per-group) pair consistent with the stimulus.

constructs.name: Representation to equation mapping
constructs.definition: The child connects an equal-group or array representation to a multiplication equation and its product within the 1-10 factor range.
constructs.observableBehavior: Child selects or assembles an equation whose factors match the represented structure and whose product matches the total.

constructs.name: Array row-column reading
constructs.definition: The child reads a rectangular array as rows of equal size and identifies rows and items per row as the two factors.
constructs.observableBehavior: Child reports row count and per-row count for an array without counting every cell one by one being required for credit.

constructs.name: Factor referent discrimination
constructs.definition: The child distinguishes what each factor counts in a specific context, including recognizing that swapping the referents changes the described situation even when the product is unchanged.
constructs.observableBehavior: Child attributes each factor to the correct quantity (groups vs. amount per group) and does not treat equal products as equal meanings.

presentationBurdenHypotheses: Text load should be low: short sentences, one stimulus per screen, so reading is not a hidden gate on math evidence (excluded construct).
Quantities should be visible and countable without fine pointer work; response mode should be selection or single small-number entry rather than dragging or drawing.
Color or grouping cues may aid parsing of equal groups, but must not by themselves signal the correct answer.

A hint affordance was favored in small-sample feedback, but hints, examples, and answer exposure are withheld during this opening evaluation to keep evidence independent; any hint affordance may only be offered after all items are recorded.
engagementHypotheses: Prior interest in harder riddles and in questioning faulty logic suggests tolerance for a discrimination item where two options share the same product; this is a hypothesis about willingness to engage, not evidence of ability.
Requesting hints when stuck suggests she may stall rather than guess; the instrument should allow an explicit 'not sure' response so stalling is recorded as missing evidence rather than forced error.
instrumentHypothesis.uncertaintyStatement: No prior mathematics performance evidence exists for this child in this domain. Difficulty placement, pacing, and item order are provisional. All engagement facts come from riddle activity and small-sample feedback and cannot predict multiplication competence. Results from this evaluation are an initial evidence sample only.

stimulus.mode: static visual plus one short sentence
stimulus.description: Four separate clusters are shown, each cluster containing exactly 6 identical dots. Sentence: 'Each bunch has the same number of dots.' No equation, no total, and no worked example is shown.
stimulus.freshness: Newly authored context (dot clusters, 4 x 6); does not reuse or paraphrase the source assignment's factor-explanation prompt.

items.prompt: How many bunches are there, and how many dots are in each bunch?

responseContract.type: two numeric entries, each a single integer 1-10
responseContract.allowedValues: integers 1-10 per field, plus an explicit 'not sure' option
responseContract.rationale: Lowest-friction mode that still preserves the two distinct quantities; avoids writing, dragging, and spelling.

correctAnswerContract.creditRule: Full credit only when both fields are correct and in the correct roles. Reversed pair (6 and 4) is scored as a distinct diagnostic outcome, not as partial credit.

difficultyBoundary.belowBoundary: Groups are visually separated and equal, so no partitioning decision is required.
difficultyBoundary.aboveBoundaryExcluded: No unequal groups, no leftover items, no two-step totals, no factors above 10.

exposureIdentity.reuseRule: This exposure identity must not recur in later items of this evaluation or in any teaching phase before evidence is recorded.

possibleConfounds: Child may count all 24 dots and infer group size by division rather than reading equal-group structure.
Reading of the single sentence could gate the response (excluded construct).
Visual clutter or cluster spacing could cause miscounting of clusters rather than a structural error.
Numeric-entry mechanics could produce an input error unrelated to mathematics.
falsifyingEvidence: Correct group and per-group values reported with reversed roles falsifies the claim that C1 role assignment is secure.
A correct total (24) reported instead of the requested pair falsifies the claim that the child parsed the requested quantities.
'Not sure' or omission falsifies any claim of available C1 evidence and marks it missing.
Correct response on this item while ITEM-2 and ITEM-3 fail falsifies a general equal-group claim and localizes evidence to separated clusters only.
items.instructionalExposure: none: no example, no hint, no feedback, no correct answer shown

stimulus.mode: static visual array plus one short sentence
stimulus.description: A rectangular array of identical squares arranged in 3 rows with 7 squares in each row. Sentence: 'Here is one rectangle of squares.' No gridlines labeled with numbers, no equation, no total shown.
stimulus.freshness: Newly authored array (3 x 7) unrelated to any source item wording.

items.prompt: How many rows are there, and how many squares are in each row?

responseContract.type: two numeric entries, each a single integer 1-10
responseContract.allowedValues: integers 1-10 per field, plus an explicit 'not sure' option
responseContract.rationale: Preserves the two array dimensions as separate quantities without requiring drawing or dragging.

correctAnswerContract.creditRule: Full credit when both fields are correct in the correct roles. The pair 7 and 3 is recorded as a role-reversal outcome, not partial credit.

difficultyBoundary.belowBoundary: Array is complete, rectangular, and unambiguous in orientation labeling (rows are horizontal).
difficultyBoundary.aboveBoundaryExcluded: No incomplete arrays, no nested arrays, no area-model conversion, no products above 100.

exposureIdentity.reuseRule: Single use within this evaluation; factor pair and structure both differ from all other items.

possibleConfounds: Row/column vocabulary may be the barrier rather than array structure (language, not mathematics).
Child may count all 21 squares one by one and still answer correctly, masking whether structure was read.
Visual scanning at the given viewport width could cause an off-by-one count.
Orientation preference may lead the child to read columns as rows.
falsifyingEvidence: Reversed pair (7 rows, 3 per row) falsifies secure row-column referent assignment while leaving structural counting intact.
Reporting 21 falsifies the claim that the child attended to the requested dimensions.
Correct here but failure on ITEM-1 falsifies a claim that equal-group parsing generalizes across separated and contiguous layouts.
'Not sure' marks C3 evidence as missing rather than absent ability.
items.instructionalExposure: none: no example, no hint, no feedback, no correct answer shown

stimulus.mode: static visual plus one short sentence
stimulus.description: Five separated equal groups are shown, each containing 3 identical items. Sentence: 'Every group holds the same amount.' No total and no equation appear in the stimulus.
stimulus.freshness: Newly authored 5 x 3 equal-group context; not a rewrite of the source prompt.

items.prompt: Choose the multiplication equation that matches what is shown.

responseContract.type: single selection from four fixed options
responseContract.additionalOption: an explicit 'not sure' choice recorded separately from the four options
responseContract.rationale: Selection is the lowest-friction mode that still requires mapping structure to both factors and the product.

correctAnswerContract.creditRule: Credit only for the option whose factors match the represented structure and whose product matches the total. No partial credit.

distractorMeanings.5 x 5 = 25: one factor duplicated; group count substituted for group size
distractorMeanings.3 x 10 = 30: correct factor present but structure and product mismatched

difficultyBoundary.belowBoundary: Only one option is structurally consistent; product arithmetic stays within a commonly memorized range so computation does not dominate.
difficultyBoundary.aboveBoundaryExcluded: No multi-step equations, no unknown-factor equations, no products above 100.

exposureIdentity.structure: separated equal groups mapped to symbolic equation
exposureIdentity.reuseRule: Options themselves constitute answer-adjacent exposure; this option set must not be reused in any later item or teaching phase.

possibleConfounds: Selection format permits guessing; a single correct choice is weak evidence (1 in 4 baseline).
Child may select by recognizing the product 15 without reading the group structure.
Option order could induce position bias.
Symbol reading (x versus +) may be the discriminating factor rather than multiplicative reasoning.
falsifyingEvidence: Selecting '5 + 3 = 8' falsifies the claim that the situation was interpreted multiplicatively.
Selecting '5 x 5 = 25' falsifies secure discrimination between number of groups and amount per group.
Correct selection combined with incorrect ITEM-1 or ITEM-2 pairs falsifies the claim that equation choice was driven by structure rather than product recognition.
Fast correct selection with latency below a plausible inspection threshold weakens, and does not confirm, the C2 claim.
items.instructionalExposure: none: no example, no hint, no feedback, no correct answer shown

stimulus.mode: two short parallel sentences, no picture
stimulus.description: Statement A: '2 baskets, and each basket holds 8 balls.' Statement B: '8 baskets, and each basket holds 2 balls.' Both statements are presented at once. No totals, equations, or pictures are shown.
stimulus.freshness: Newly authored referent-swap contrast; the source assignment's explanation prompt is not reused in wording or format.

items.prompt: Do these two statements describe the same situation? Then say how many baskets Statement A describes.

responseContract.type: one selection plus one numeric entry
responseContract.rationale: Avoids requiring written explanation, which would convert the item into a writing measure, while still separating referent meaning from bare product equality.

correctAnswerContract.creditRule: Full credit requires both fields correct. Selecting 'same' is scored as evidence that equal products were treated as equal meanings, regardless of the numeric field.
correctAnswerContract.note: Both statements yield the product 16; product equality is deliberately not the discriminating feature.

difficultyBoundary.belowBoundary: Only two statements are compared; no third case, no justification required, no symbolic equation to parse.
difficultyBoundary.aboveBoundaryExcluded: No formal commutativity statement required, no explanation writing, no factors above 10.

exposureIdentity.structure: verbal referent swap with constant product
exposureIdentity.reuseRule: Single use; the swap structure is the sharpest evidence in this set and must not be previewed earlier in the sequence.

possibleConfounds: The word 'same' is ambiguous between same total and same situation; a 'same' response may reflect interpretation of the question rather than factor-referent confusion.
Reading load is highest in this item and could gate the response (excluded construct).
Child may already know commutativity and answer 'same' for a mathematically defensible product-based reason.
Order of Statement A and B could bias which referent is anchored.
falsifyingEvidence: Selecting 'same' falsifies the claim of secure factor-referent discrimination, but is ambiguous with a product-based reading of 'same' and therefore requires a follow-up disambiguation probe before any C4 claim.
Correct 'different' with an incorrect basket count falsifies the claim that the specific referents were tracked.
Correct response here combined with role reversals in ITEM-1 or ITEM-2 falsifies a general C4 claim and confines it to verbal contexts.
'Not sure' on either field marks C4 evidence as missing.
items.instructionalExposure: none: no example, no hint, no feedback, no correct answer shown

completionRule.sequenceRationale: Prerequisite-first ordering: equal-group structure, then array reading, then representation-to-equation mapping, then factor-referent discrimination. Later items must not reveal structure needed by earlier ones.

administration.independentEvidenceWindow: All four items are administered before any teaching, worked example, hint, feedback, or correct-answer exposure.
administration.hintAffordanceAllowedAfter: all four item responses are recorded

completionCriteria: Evaluation is complete when each of ITEM-1 through ITEM-4 has a recorded outcome from the set {correct, incorrect, not_sure, omitted, abandoned}.
A response of 'not sure', omission, or abandonment is a valid terminal outcome for that item and is recorded as missing evidence for its construct, never as a failure of ability.
Evaluation is also complete if the child stops early; all unreached items are recorded as missing evidence and the constructs they target remain unresolved.

scoringPolicy.noMasteryDeclaration: No outcome combination, including four correct responses, may be reported as mastery, proficiency, or a settled skill claim. One item per construct is a single observation sample.
confoundGating: A correct response with latency below the inspection threshold is downgraded to evidence_ambiguous.
Any item flagged for reading, input, or pointer interference is downgraded to evidence_ambiguous and its construct is treated as unresolved.
ITEM-4 'same' responses are always flagged evidence_ambiguous pending a disambiguation probe.
crossItemConsistencyChecks: Role reversal appearing in both ITEM-1 and ITEM-2 indicates a candidate referent-assignment gap that ITEM-4 must corroborate or contradict.
Correct ITEM-3 with incorrect ITEM-1 and ITEM-2 indicates probable product recognition rather than structural mapping.

completionRule.outputOfEvaluation: A per-construct evidence map (C1, C2, C3, C4) with each construct labeled supported-provisionally, contradicted, ambiguous, or missing, plus the list of confound flags raised. No instructional plan is produced by this artifact.
prohibitions: no world, character, setting, or narrative
no game type or named mechanic
no visual style, theme, or art direction beyond neutral countable shapes
no sound, music, reward, points, badges, or streaks
no HTML, markup, or implementation code
no mastery, proficiency, or grade-level-attainment claim
no teaching, modeling, or answer exposure inside the evaluation window

evidenceRequiredNext: Disambiguation probe for ITEM-4 when 'same' is selected: a non-teaching follow-up that separates 'same total' from 'same situation' without revealing the correct answer.
A second, structurally different observation per construct before any construct may move beyond provisional status; one item is an insufficient sample.
A no-picture equal-group item to test whether C1 depends on visual separation of groups.
An unknown-factor probe (total and one factor given, other factor requested) to test whether C2 mapping is bidirectional or only representation-to-equation.
A column-reading array probe to test whether C3 is orientation-dependent rather than structural.
Confound-isolation checks: a read-aloud or reduced-text version of the same construct to determine whether any incorrect response was gated by reading load rather than mathematics.
Input-mode check: confirmation that numeric entry and selection mechanics did not produce recorded errors unrelated to mathematics.
Latency baselines for this child on a non-mathematical selection task, to calibrate the inspection threshold used in guessing control.
Repeat observation on a separate occasion to distinguish stable evidence from single-session variation.
Post-evaluation-only: whether an available hint changes performance, recorded strictly after independent evidence is closed and reported separately from opening evidence.
